To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we achieve photometric calibration of PS1 to ∼ 1% over much of the survey, and we find that the PS1 system throughput is very close to the design value.
we have performed an internal calibration of PanSTARRS 1 photometry, using repeat observations of stars, that achieves relative precision of <10 mmag in grizP1 and <20 mmag in yP1.
we have developed and implemented a calibration scheme that achieves relative photometric precision < 10 mmags in g, r and iP1, ∼ 10mmags in z and y and absolute calibration precision ∼ 2mmags.

the study of the structure and dynamics of the solar corona and the Sun-Earth system, and the development of new instrumentation for space and ground-based observations.
the development of a novel, non-invasive, optical method of measuring the mechanical properties of materials.
the study of the physical properties of stars and the interstellar medium in the Magellanic Clouds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PS1 is a very good photometric survey.
the photometric calibration of PS1 is good, and that it is good enough for the science that PS1 was designed to perform.

the PS1 photometric calibration is now at the level where the survey can deliver the science that it was designed to do, and that the calibration has the precision and accuracy to enable a wide variety of science that was not originally anticipated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated that we can achieve 10% photometry over most of the sky with the PS1 survey.
the PS1 system is capable of producing photometry of unprecedented accuracy over large areas of the sky.
PS1 photometry is as good as or better than SDSS photometry.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PS1 is capable of achieving photometric precision of < 1% in g, r and iP1 over much of the northern sky.
PS1 is a very stable photometric survey, and that the system is capable of producing photometry with an absolute precision of ∼ 1%, even in the most challenging conditions.
PS1 is a photometrically stable survey that will enable < 0.1 mag precision in its 3σ photometry for stars brighter than r ∼ 20.5.
